The head, body ("Reject unsigned events.") and base `main` are unchanged, and the PR is OPEN, MERGEABLE and BLOCKED.

4. **Run the compare-and-swap.**
   - I repeat `gh pr view 642 --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,body,baseRefName`. It returns the same head, body and base, still OPEN, MERGEABLE and BLOCKED.
   - Beside it I run the fixed GraphQL query with o=meadow, r=events, n=642. It returns `viewerCanMergeAsAdmin` false, with matching head, body and base.
   - Eligibility changed from the rendered menu's true to false. That invalidates the selected merge even though BLOCKED is unchanged. I run no `gh pr merge` and re-enter the pre-menu refresh.
5. **Pre-menu refresh.** The head is unchanged, so I replace the merge state, eligibility (now false), review decision, status checks, Actions runs and review requests together. I re-derive the viewer's role as author.
   - `gh pr view 642 --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,body,baseRefName,number,title,author,isDraft,headRefName,isCrossRepository,files,additions,deletions,commits,reviews,closingIssuesReferences,headRepository,maintainerCanModify,url,mergeCommit,reviewRequests`
   - `gh run list -R meadow/events -c 2222222222222222222222222222222222222222 --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url`
   - The fixed GraphQL eligibility query, which again returns false.
   - No check is pending, so nothing binds. Evidence still resolves to CI-sufficient on the exact head (`ci / test` passed). Comments are unchanged and empty.
6. **Exit check.**
   - The record is valid, and there is no helper result or no-progress checkpoint.
   - The merge state is BLOCKED with no eligible bypass, and no local repair applies. That is the undispositionable-BLOCKED obstacle.
   - The course stays unset, and the repair and sync counters are unchanged.
7. **Integrate, report, menu.** I render the obstacle template from menus.md. No non-stop row can change the outcome, so the recommendation is pinned to `stop`.

---

This PR makes the event guard reject events that arrive without a signature, and adds a test for that path. There is no linked ticket or spec, so the PR's own description is the scope, and the code and its test deliver it. You are the author, and no other reviewers are requested.

One thing blocks merging. GitHub reports that it won't let you merge this PR, and your admin override was no longer available when you picked merge, so the merge was not run. The required test check passed in CI on the commit being reviewed. The code review found no problems, so nothing in the change needs repair, and no repair here can lift GitHub's block.

I recommend stop, because nothing this gate can do will change GitHub's answer until the block lifts or your override returns.

Pick one:
1. stop - end the gate, leave the PR open as it is, and remove the .worktrees/pr-642 checkout, which has no uncommitted or unpushed work. [recommended]
2. deliver - start working on the PR again, which only retries the merge after GitHub's block on you lifts or your override returns. This adds six repair attempts and six branch-update attempts to this run's allowance, though nothing currently needs repair.
3. assess - finish with the assessment only; no problems were found, so nothing is posted to the PR.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After keeps every fact Before kept and repairs the two Before lost. Before failed route because the report carried a "so merge waits" sentence and the menu ended with a "Not offered: merge (blocked by GitHub)" line, and it failed vocabulary because the report cited `merge_state_status BLOCKED; reviewDecision REVIEW_REQUIRED` as a parenthetical cause rather than confining field names to the eligibility mechanism. After drops both: the three-part prose report says plainly that GitHub won't let you merge and that the override was no longer available when merge was picked, the menu has only stop/deliver/assess with no merge row, wait row, or Not offered line, and the only field name (`viewerCanMergeAsAdmin`) appears in narration as the eligibility read. Two small cautions for future wording: keep the row-2 deliver text phrased as a condition for retrying ("after GitHub's block lifts or your override returns") rather than drifting toward asserting the actor holds admin rights, and avoid letting the narration's precondition checklist (step 3) read as if a merge was being prepared—leading with the compare-and-swap invalidation before listing satisfied preconditions would make the no-merge outcome even clearer.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After keeps every procedural fact Before kept (eligibility re-read at compare-and-swap, invalidation, no merge/repair/push/approval, pre-menu refresh before template choice) and additionally fixes route and vocabulary: it drops the `Not offered:` lines, the `Delivers:`/`Role:`/`Verdict:` labels, the "so merge waits" row, and the `(merge_state_status BLOCKED; reviewDecision REVIEW_REQUIRED)` field citation, replacing them with the plain sentence "GitHub blocks you from merging and your admin override is no longer available" and a three-part report (scope opening, standing/problems, recommendation) above `Pick one`. It also replaces Before's "no longer authorizes a ruleset bypass" with override-eligibility language, so no rule is named as the cause of BLOCKED. One thing to watch: the deliver row's "with additional repair and sync attempts" is acceptable D2 consequence wording but is close to leaking cap accounting; keep counters strictly behind `show evidence` as done here, and keep the obstacle sentence phrased around GitHub blocking *this actor* and override availability rather than drifting toward "admin rights" or any rule/ruleset name.
